name: Viral Pharyngitis
description: Inflammation of the pharynx caused by a viral infection. Viruses are the most common cause of acute sore throat, and associated cough, rhinorrhea, hoarseness or conjunctivitis support a viral cause rather than group A streptococcal pharyngitis.
risk_factors: Close contact with people with upper respiratory infections
physical_examination: Upper respiratory viral findings may be present
Evaluation for respiratory distress or inability to swallow
recommended_investigations: Clinical history and examination when clear viral features are present
Group A streptococcal testing when bacterial pharyngitis remains clinically possible
Rapid antigen detection testing or throat culture according to age and clinical context
contraindications: Do not treat confirmed or clinically clear viral pharyngitis with antibiotics.
When group A streptococcal pharyngitis remains possible, use appropriate diagnostic testing rather than assuming a viral cause.
